calls.reason: The packet holds no usable evidence. The searches found only total capex reports, not AI-specific capex, and whether the companies kept their promises was not established.

The deadline is the end of 2026 and has not passed. OpenAI's June 2026 statement says engineering samples are running in the lab, but no volume production or deployment has been reported, and 'build' is ambiguous.
The only evidence is Menlo's $12B consumer AI spending estimate, far narrower than the industry. No media examples showing current revenue presented as about $1 trillion were found.

Base44's founder reported a profitable May 2025 and TechCrunch called it profitable, but that is one unverified month from a firm that may sit outside the group Zitron meant. It is not clear enough to call.
Meta's filing guided $64–72B in 2025 capex and Alphabet guided about $75B. Both totals fall materially short of 'nearly a hundred billion dollars each', so the per-company figure does not hold.

The forecast has no deadline. Korean news stories document individual losses in chip-stock retirement funds, while Fidelity data show US balances rising, so there is no evidence of widespread wrecked retirements.
